image_description: A medium shot of a smiling man wearing a black academic gown with velvet bars on the sleeves, indicating a doctoral degree. He is wearing a mortarboard cap (partially visible) and holding a white rolled document or diploma in his right hand. The background consists of beige curtains and some dark equipment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flowing full-length garment with rectangular silhouette draping from shoulders to ankles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The garment exhibits the characteristic loose, rectangular drape of an academic gown, covering the torso and extending downwards out of frame.
The gown opens at the front, revealing the attire underneath, and maintains general bilateral symmetry in its cut.
The fabric hangs loosely, hiding the specific shape of the wearer's torso and legs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide open sleeves extending well below hand level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the sleeves are wide, they do not extend 'well below hand level' in a hanging manner; the wearer's hands are protruding from the ends, suggesting standard length or that the sleeves are pushed up/interacting with the hands, rather than the distinctive 'bell sleeve' drape described in the strict taxonomy.
The vertical edges of the front opening are visible.
A collared shirt and tie are clearly visible underneath the gown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fabric appears opaque, heavy, and non-reflective, consistent with traditional gown materials.
No specular highlights or shiny textures are observed on the main body of the gown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Similar to the functional component check, the sleeves terminate at or near the wrists where the hands emerge, lacking the exaggerated drape specified in the ground truth description.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white object held in the right hand lacks clear definition; it blends slightly into the fingers, appearing somewhat melted or indistinct, typical of AI generation struggling with hand-object interaction.
The left hand appears anatomically awkward; the fingers are short, stubby, and lack distinct separation, with the thumb area merging into the palm/sleeve cuff.
The vertical folds of the curtain behind the subject show slight waviness and inconsistency in perspective convergence, though this could also be due to the physical nature of the curtain.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of academic regalia (doctoral vs. bachelor/master) based on sleeve bars and hood presence.
To audit the structural integrity of the hands and arms, specifically checking for missing digits or fusion artifacts which were visually suspected.
To verify the separation between the gown sleeves and the hands, and the gown hem against the background, checking for edge bleeding.
To assess overall coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts missed by specific auditors.

focus_areas: Interaction between hands and held object
Sleeve structure and velvet bar alignment
Edge sharpness between gown and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the hands. AI models often fail at rendering hands inside sleeves or holding objects. Verify if the 'melted' appearance of the right hand's object and the stubby left fingers are genuine artifacts or just low-resolution compression. Also, evaluate if the failure to meet the 'sleeves extending well below hand level' checkpoint is a class mismatch (e.g., wrong type of gown) or an AI generation error in proportion.
